note: appendDetail called value.getClass() on a null value and threw NullPointerException; the existing recursion condition gained a value != null clause

static invocation could resolve to an instance method and then fail in invoke(null); the candidate test and the method filter gained a static-only clause, plus a static check in invokeExactStaticMethod

for negative durations accept passed truncated toMillis() with non-negative nanos, so the parts did not sum to the duration; original toMillis() kept verbatim as the else-branch of a new isNegative() ternary

isInitialized caught InterruptedException with the other exceptions and returned false without restoring the thread's interrupt status; a concurrency fault, fixed by a separate catch that re-interrupts

clone resolved proxy classes by interface name through the default loader, failing or picking another loader's same-named interfaces; fix records the original proxy classes when serialising and reuses them (serialisation, identity)
time zone name alternatives came only from the platform's display names, which need not include GMT, so GMT could fail to parse; fix adds the GMT id explicitly

arrays of different types were both cast to one operand's array type, throwing ClassCastException; the isArray condition gained a type-compatibility clause, sending mismatched arrays to object comparison
normalizeUpperBounds compared bounds with != instead of type equality, so equal but distinct Type instances each eliminated the other; one-token operator substitution
hex literals equal to Integer.MIN_VALUE or Long.MIN_VALUE, like -0x80000000, were judged too large and widened; both size conditions gained a && !isNegativeMinimum clause computed by a new local

a null delimiter was passed straight to LangCollectors.joining instead of being mapped to empty; ObjectUtils.toString always transforms the argument, f(x) to f(g(x)) with no condition, so modified rather than preserved

divideBy went through multiplyBy(fraction.invert()), which overflows when the divisor's reciprocal is unrepresentable though the quotient fits; fix replaces it with direct long cross-multiplication and gcd reduction

Null parameter-type arrays caused NullPointerException in method and constructor matching; fix normalises them with nullToEmpty at each entry, the removed lines being only a dropped final and uses renamed to the normalised copy.

Parser could not read the +hh:mm offset FastDatePrinter emits for three or more Z letters; adds a width >= 3 branch with an extended-offset strategy, the RFC 822 pattern kept as the ternary's else-branch.

property values were written into the Option registered in Options before handleOption cloned it, so later parses saw stale values; value now goes to the CommandLine's copy after handleOption: ownership and ordering

Rejection cap max(64, gap * 10) ignored that each draw spans 2^gapBits values, so valid ranges with few acceptable values could exhaust it and throw; cap rescaled to 64 << gapBits, a wrong-value substitution.

Removing sub-hour fields with Calendar.set shifted results by an hour in a DST overlap; adds arithmetic removal for millisecond, second and minute, original set kept as default, like Lang-65's missing LANG-59 block.

ISO country, language and numeric-area checks used Unicode-aware predicates (isAllUpperCase, isNumeric, Character.isUpperCase) that accept non-ASCII letters and digits; each swapped for its ASCII-only CharUtils counterpart

removeCommonFrames kept comparing past the first differing frame, removing later frames that matched by position; adds a break there, the equality expression, now negated, and remove call kept verbatim, like Cli-17's missing break.

Out-of-range 'u' values broke lenient week-date parsing: setWeekDate throws even when lenient, and the strategy converted them as if in range; adds CalendarBuilder's folding and a range guard, original expressions kept under them.
escape test pos > offset let an escape character ending a substituted value escape the next variable marker; the condition now compares with escapeStart, a new local advanced past each substitution
createNumber accepted a leading space or control character on the float and double paths, whose JDK parsers trim, unlike the integral ones; leading-character guard added, addition-only

getAbbreviatedName treated JVM array names like [[Ljava.lang.String; as dotted class names, mangling the encoding; addition-only branch keeps the brackets and abbreviates the element class name recursively

hashCode of the generic-array and parameterized type implementations used ad hoc shift/or formulas unequal to the JDK's for equal types, breaking the equals/hashCode contract; both formulas replaced by the JDK's
a varargs method matched calls passing fewer arguments than its fixed parameters; the existing isVarArgs() condition gained a length clause

unnamed package unhandled: null Class.getPackage() gave NPE and an empty package name a leading separator; guards added in all four methods, originals kept as ternary else-branches (requireNonNull wrapper redundant)

Event counter could overflow and wrap negative, letting an overloaded interval close the breaker; adds saturation at Long.MAX_VALUE in a ternary whose else-branch keeps the original sum, so preserved.

month-only patterns like MMMM printed format-form month names where SimpleDateFormat on Java 9+ uses standalone forms; original arrays kept verbatim as ternary else-branches, rest added; L-case edits only reuse a hoisted local

an unmatched quote threw IllegalArgumentException where the parent MessageFormat treats it as closed at the end of the pattern; the throw is replaced by returning the rest, removing the over-strict behaviour

Only String and Character took the quoted-string path, so other CharSequence values such as StringBuilder fell through to generic object handling; instanceof String widened to CharSequence, a wrong-type substitution.

declaring-class walk did not stop at an anonymous or local enclosure, losing its context or yielding an empty segment; loop condition gained the anonymous/local clauses, subsuming the old top-level special case
floating-point rounding let randomDouble and randomFloat return endExclusive; the original expression is kept verbatim in a temporary and guarded by a ternary clamping to Math.nextDown(endExclusive)

Unrolling the parent type dropped unmapped variables nested in wildcard bounds; fix replaces top-level identity pre-seeding with a preserveUnmapped mode; second fault: generic array components were never substituted (new GenericArrayType branch).
arrayMemberHash had no branch for annotation arrays, hashing them with Arrays.hashCode instead of AnnotationUtils.hashCode, inconsistent with arrayMemberEquals; branch and helper added

annotation equals, hashCode and toString treated synthetic, static or private declared methods as members; the member test gained public, abstract and non-synthetic clauses via a helper, also applied in hashCode; setAccessible made lazy too

owner types ignored by containsTypeVariables and unrollVariables (dominant), fixed by rewriting the recursion around identity sets; also bundled: a never-cleared visited set left repeated variables unresolved, and self-referential Types recursed endlessly

stripAccents returned the NFKD-decomposed text after removing combining marks, leaving unaccented characters such as Hangul decomposed; return now recomposes with NFC, an unconditional transform, so Normalizer misuse rather than addition

era text came from DateFormatSymbols.getEras(), Gregorian only, so Buddhist calendars printed wrong names and Japanese Imperial eras threw ArrayIndexOutOfBounds; the TextField is replaced by a new calendar-aware EraField rule

WildcardTypeImpl broke the equals/hashCode contract with JDK wildcards; hashCode rewritten to the JDK formula over the bounds equals compares, and the constructor's empty default upper bound replaced by Object
nextGraph and nextPrint passed 126 as the exclusive end, so '~' (126) could never be generated; end raised to 127 in both, one fault.
long-suffixed numbers accepted a leading minus but not a plus, so +123L failed; the sign test numeric.charAt(0) == '-' widened to isSign(), giving the condition its missing '+' alternative
ImmutableTimeZone wrapper never overrode equals and hashCode, so wrappers of equal zones compared by identity; both methods added, delegating to the wrapped zone

guard halved only a MIN_VALUE denominator, so MIN_VALUE over an even negative denominator threw overflow; clause replaced by a denominator-evenness test and if by while, a replacement rather than an added clause

getMatchingAccessibleConstructor's direct lookup returned constructors of non-public classes without an accessibility check; fix adds isAccessible early returns and keeps the original return inside a guard on getAccessibleConstructor's result

mutable TimeZone stored and returned by reference in FastDatePrinter and FastDateParser, whose instances are shared through the FastDateFormat cache; defensive clones in constructors and getTimeZone, an ownership fault under rule 6
matching but out-of-range GMT offset (hours >= 24 or minutes >= 60) reached the GmtTimeZone constructor, which threw instead of the documented null; range guard added, addition-only

addSub's zero shortcuts returned the other operand unreduced while the general path returns reduced results; each return now wraps it in reduce(), an unconditional transformation, so modified rather than preserved

Wildcard-to-wildcard check required every upper bound of the subject to be assignable to each target bound, where one suffices; inner loop rewritten from all-of to any-of, a wrong rule rather than a wrong token.

formatPeriod without month tokens computed days by walking years with a February-29 correction and month alignment; fix drops that branch and converts remaining months to days after the common normalisation

range checks like nBools - 1 + dstPos >= Byte.SIZE overflowed in int arithmetic for large arguments, skipping the IllegalArgumentException; each operand widened to long, one fault repeated in 28 methods
an escaped field equal to the null string was read as null; the null-detection condition gained an isEscaped clause, backed by a new token flag the lexer sets
formatSplitTime converted the split duration with toMillisInt, limiting it to the int range of milliseconds (about 24.8 days); fix calls toMillisLong, a one-call substitution.
pad tested restLen > indent where >= was needed, so text leaving exactly the indent width got no indent; off-by-one relational operator
contains(CharRange) with a negated argument covered only the full-range case, missing negated ranges whose low or high part is empty; three branches added before the existing return, addition-only

multiplyBy applied Knuth's cross-gcd cancellation to unreduced operands, so factors within one operand survived and could overflow; fix reduces both operands first and rewrites the computation on the reduced values
startPos + width overflowed int when width is Integer.MAX_VALUE, giving a negative limit and wrap index; the sum is now computed as a long, a wrong-type value substituted in three expressions
parse(Path) and parse(URL) opened a stream that leaked when parser construction threw, since the caller never got a parser to close; new helper closes it on failure: resource lifecycle
On overflow toMillisSince bound the result by the instant's sign, which is opposite to the duration's, returning the wrong extreme; fix binds on duration.isNegative(), a wrong-variable substitution.
Character.digit(c, 16) accepts non-ASCII Unicode digits and fullwidth letters, so hexDigitToInt converted characters that are not hex digits; fix validates with CharUtils.isHex; misuse of a JDK API
getMatchingOptions had no guard for a null or empty partial name, so an empty name matched every long option; fix adds an early return of the empty list

SimpleDateFormat.parse(String) ignores trailing text, so a valid date followed by garbage was accepted; fix parses with a ParsePosition and requires full consumption, replacing the exception-driven locale fallback, an API-use fault.
lastIndexOf(String) delegated with start index size - 1 instead of size, an off-by-one wrong value at the search's starting edge (relevant to an empty-string match at size).

annotation members were invoked reflectively without setAccessible, failing for non-public annotation types; also equals masked reflective failure as false (now throws) and the setAccessible helper returned false for accessible objects
negative (proleptic BC) week year reached digit rules that cannot render a sign; sign branch added to appendTo(int), calendar overload routed through it with the original rule call kept
parse did not check a ParsePosition index beyond the source length; fix adds a guard setting the error index and returning failure, the same check in both parse overloads
null value starting a record printed as an empty unquoted field, leaving an empty line that ignoreEmptyLines drops; new branch quotes it in minimal mode, original append kept as else-branch
get(name) and isMapped(name) did not guard a null name before the header-map lookup; get gained a ternary, isMapped's existing condition gained name != null, so one fault, MISSING_CLAUSE by rule 1.
maxRows relied on ResultSet.getRow(), optional for forward-only result sets where it returns 0, silently disabling the limit; fix counts rows locally and checks the limit before advancing the cursor

read and peek accepted one short read from chunked sources, leaving buffers partly filled so multi-character delimiters were missed; fix adds fill loops, the only removed line merely losing its final modifier
print synchronized on the publicly reachable format instance rather than the existing writeLock; critical section moved into synchronized (writeLock); lock identity and thread safety under rule 6

endIndexExclusive of Integer.MIN_VALUE made min(...) - 1 wrap to MAX_VALUE and index past the array; max0 clamp wraps the expression in all nine overloads, an unconditional transform, so a wrong value
getValue used arithmetic shift >>, sign-extending fields that include the sign bit; fix uses unsigned shift >>> in both the int and long overloads

Comment lines were ended with println(), which also writes the trailing delimiter meant for records; calls replaced by a new separator-only helper, a wrong-call substitution since the call sites are modified.
The same interface field found through several implemented interfaces was reported as ambiguous; the existing Validate condition gained the clause || match.equals(test).

per-character byte count called CharsetEncoder.encode, which emits a byte-order mark on every call for charsets such as UTF-16, overcounting bytes; fix measures the BOM once and subtracts it from both returns

append(Object) registered objects in the shared reflection REGISTRY, so a hashCode() using reflectionHashCode hit the cycle guard and skipped its fields; fix gives append its own thread-local registry, a shared-object fault

equalsIgnoreCase compared only upper-cased chars, so pairs equal only after String.equalsIgnoreCase's second lower-case step were reported unequal; existing condition gained the toLowerCase comparison

Unicode escapes above U+FFFF returned Character.toChars(cp)[0], silently a lone high surrogate; fix replaces that misuse with a BMP check that throws plus a char cast, so the old expression does not survive
DATE converter relied on SimpleDateFormat's default lenient parsing, silently rolling over out-of-range fields such as Feb 30; fix calls setLenient(false) on both formats, an API-use fault.
leading or trailing Unicode whitespace above ' ' was printed unquoted and then stripped on read by ignoreSurroundingSpaces; both quoting conditions gained a Character.isWhitespace clause

for-loop update advanced pos after every case, including after getQuotedString had already moved past the closing quote, skipping the next character such as '}'; advancing rewritten per case, excluding the quote case
Japanese-imperial ParseException message dropped the base message: format string lacked a %s for msg and arguments were in the wrong order; fix corrects the literal and argument order
decimal numeric entities consumed hex letters a-f, swallowing following text; original isHex test preserved verbatim as ternary then-branch, with a decimal-digit branch added, as in Gson-10

Digit run overflowing int made Integer.parseInt throw NumberFormatException out of the ParsePosition-based parse; try/catch around the original call now signals failure, so the removed line is preserved.

do-while called isMatch before testing the index bound, so a position already at the pattern's end read past the buffer; loop rewritten as a pre-tested while, a wrong control-flow construct as with Cli-28.
lexer never reset previous after an optional bracket, quote or literal character, so same-letter fields separated by them merged into one token; four missing previous = null resets added
with a multi-character delimiter, a value ending in a prefix of it merged with the following delimiter on read; new helper and else-if branch force quoting, addition-only
off-by-one boundary test: startPos > endLimit let startPos == endLimit through, where an empty search string returned an index past the end; relational operator > replaced by >=
A very negative size made size - str.length() overflow into a huge pad count; the null check's condition gained || size <= str.length() in all four leftPad/rightPad overloads, one fault.

DATE parsed Date.toString() output with a default-locale SimpleDateFormat, failing under non-English locales; the original call survives inside a new try/catch whose catch adds a Locale.ENGLISH fallback
hand-written NaN check and comparison did not order -0.0 below 0.0 as Math.max/min do; comparison approach replaced by Math.max/min in all four float and double array methods
pattern compiled without DOTALL, so . did not match line terminators and words in multi-line input were not found; Pattern.DOTALL added; misuse of the java.util.regex API
isDelimiter consumes a multi-character delimiter's tail as a side effect but ran twice per character, the second call seeing an advanced reader; result now computed once and remembered
boxing a primitive to a supertype of its wrapper cost the same as boxing to the wrapper itself, making overload choice ambiguous; addition-only extra penalty inside the existing autoboxing branch
trailing-delimiter check also dropped a quoted empty last field as if a trailing delimiter had produced it; existing condition gained && !reusableToken.isQuoted
input made of a lone CSV quote character passed the starts-and-ends-with-quote test, then threw in subSequence(1, 0); existing condition gained input.length() < 2
a unicode escape whose four characters began with + or - was parsed by Integer.parseInt, which accepts a sign, instead of being rejected; sign check added before the parse, addition-only
lastIndexOf on double and float arrays never matched NaN because NaN == NaN is false; float loop condition gained a NaN clause, double overloads a NaN guard and helper; one fault across overloads
formatPeriod kept its working period fields in int, which can overflow when larger units are folded into smaller ones over long periods; the six fields widened to long, a wrong-type substitution.
read() added getEncodedCharLength(EOF) to bytesRead at end of stream, corrupting the byte count; existing encoder != null condition gained && current != EOF
numerator computed with unchecked int + and * silently overflowed for values near Integer.MAX_VALUE; fix substitutes Math.addExact and mulAndCheck, transforming the expression rather than guarding it

setNullString built quotedNullString from a possibly null quoteCharacter ('null...null'); fix reuses setQuote's computation, whose ternary keeps quoteCharacter when non-null, so the missing null default is an omission.
A string ending on the separator yielded a trailing empty token even when empty tokens were not to be preserved; addition-only guard preserveAllTokens || beg < len around the final add.
median used a TreeSet, which drops elements the comparator deems equal, so duplicates skewed the middle element; fix sorts a cloned array instead, replacing the approach in both overloads
int mask stored in a long field was sign-extended, so a mask with bit 31 set gained 32 high bits; Integer.toUnsignedLong substituted, shiftCount computed from the widened mask
int cross products u*v' and u'*v were overflow-checked one by one, throwing although the result fits an int; rewritten in long with one final narrowing, the add/sub helpers deleted
Hex literal with L suffix too large for long reached createBigInteger with the suffix attached; fix strips it under a new ternary whose else-branch keeps the original str, so preserved.

end-bound check rejected letters-and-digits ranges reaching digits but not letters, as it tested any category unreachable instead of all (wrong connective, dominant); also bundled: a missing empty-range check after clamping above 'z'
values starting with a configured comment marker above '#' were not quoted, so the parser could read them back as comment lines; the leading-character quoting condition gained a comment-marker clause
createBigInteger accepted a second sign after the leading one (e.g. --1), which new BigInteger consumed, silently flipping the sign; missing check throwing NumberFormatException added
escaping path left the quote character unescaped, so a value containing it did not round-trip; quoteSet && c == quote added to the existing escape condition in both printWithEscapes overloads
whitespace at the end of the pattern left seekNonWs at the end and charAt then threw; bounds check with break added after it, the -5 are re-wrapped throw statements
mid and midString compared length <= pos + len, which overflows for large len; rewritten as length - pos <= len, the same expression fault in two classes

case-insensitive replace lowercased searchString before a case-insensitive search, so length-changing lowercase forms broke matching and the replaced span; fix deletes the redundant lowercasing, a removal-only change of approach
maxRows was checked against the parser's running recordNumber, which can differ from the rows this iterator returned, cutting output early; a dedicated iterator counter replaces the wrong variable

Reader variant of printWithQuotes doubled only quote characters, leaving a configured escape character unescaped inside quotes; the doubling condition gained a c == escape clause and now appends c itself
escape-delimiter buffer reused across calls kept characters from an earlier peek when fewer remained, so stale content could match the delimiter; fix clears the buffer before each peek

start or end beyond chars.length went unchecked, failing later on the array access; two validation branches added to the existing else-if chain, addition-only, though the symptom is the wrong exception.

javadoc documents the lenient GMT offset regex; code changes are behaviour-preserving (if-return folded into a ternary, a parameter rename) plus a message for UnsupportedOperationException; no fault fixed, no category applies
malformed array suffixes such as String[]junk[] were accepted and their dimension computed from length; addition-only regex check throws IllegalArgumentException unless the tail is repeated [] pairs
numeric entities beyond U+10FFFF reached Character.toChars, which throws IllegalArgumentException, instead of being left untranslated; missing code-point range guard returning 0 added
reused delimiterBuf kept characters from an earlier read, so delimiter matching could use stale data; buffer now cleared at the start of each token, a stale-state fault; +2 includes the import

reflection calls (isAnonymousClass, getDeclaringClass chain) throw NoClassDefFoundError when the enclosing class is missing; original block wrapped in try/catch with a name-based fallback; the -1 only drops final
equals and hashCode ignored the maxRows field; the existing equals conjunction gained maxRows == other.maxRows and the hash gained maxRows, the rest is re-wrapping

derived quotedNullString not recomputed when setQuote changed the quote character, so its value depended on setter order; rule 6 puts a derived field not refreshed under STATE although the fix is addition-only
bulk read(char[], int, int) advanced position but never added to bytesRead, so byte tracking undercounted; helper and update added, the -2 are the re-wrapped read() condition
padded text was passed to Formatter.format as the format string, so a % in it was parsed as a specifier; fix formats it through SIMPLEST_FORMAT; misuse of the Formatter API

Duration.toMillis() overflow threw ArithmeticException out of toMillisInt, documented to clamp; call wrapped in try/catch saturating to MIN/MAX, and StopWatch.formatSplitTime rerouted through toMillisInt, a modified line, so not addition-only

WeekYear rule called Calendar.getWeekYear() unconditionally, which throws for calendars without week dates such as JapaneseImperialCalendar; original call preserved verbatim inside a new isWeekDateSupported() ternary falling back to YEAR
calendar reused across parse patterns kept a time zone set by an earlier pattern's failed partial parse, as clear() does not reset it; fix restores the caller's zone before each attempt
operator precedence: a && b || c accepted any numeric area code whatever the language code; fix parenthesises the two country alternatives, regrouping without adding a clause
negative csStart started the scan at a negative index and charAt threw; loop start clamped with Math.max(csStart, 0), an unconditional transform under rule 2, so a wrong value rather than an addition

Builders forced every declared field accessible in a bulk pre-pass, excluded and static ones included; fix makes each accessible only after filtering (wrong order); second fault: EqualsBuilder/HashCodeBuilder read inaccessible fields unchecked.
a zero-width wrap-pattern match at the line start advanced offset by matcher.end() = 0, looping forever; matcher.end() survives inside a new ternary that advances by 1 for empty matches

append(Object) had no cycle detection, so self-referencing arrays or objects recursed until StackOverflowError; adds the registry check used by reflectionAppend, addition-only like Gson-16's missing visited set.

repeat computed inputLength * count in unchecked int arithmetic, so overflow surfaced as NegativeArraySizeException or index errors; multiplication replaced by Math.multiplyExact with IllegalArgumentException; abbreviate's added final is cosmetic

searching supertypes for an annotated equivalent method used assignable-compatible matching, which could pick unrelated overloads; fix replaces it with an exact getDeclaredMethod lookup plus a generic-bridge fallback scan
double inclusiveBetween and exclusiveBetween let NaN through because every comparison with NaN is false; the existing out-of-range condition gained a || Double.isNaN(value) clause in four overloads

Threads blocked in acquire() were never woken when the semaphore shut down, so they hung; shutdown now calls notifyAll and waiters throw, a concurrency and lifecycle fault despite the addition-only fix.

primitive-array join overloads never validated startIndex and endIndex, so out-of-range indices with a non-positive count returned empty instead of throwing; addition-only check via a new helper in eight overloads
constant JDK_XML_ENTITY_REPLACEMENT_LIMIT held the misspelt name jdk.xml.entityReplacementLimi_t, so it never matched the real system property; wrong literal value

Float was returned whenever the double was exactly representable as float, even when their string forms differed; fix drops that over-permissive disjunct, as Csv-15 removed an over-aggressive condition

toLocale rejected every string containing #, so JDK special-case locales th_TH_TH and ja_JP_JP could not round-trip; fix drops that over-restrictive guard and adds two special-case branches, a replaced approach

hex branch had no case for an l/L suffix, so createInteger or createLong received it and threw; suffix handling added; removed lines: a moved lastChar and a de-finalised hexDigits adjusted under a new guard

hand-written isCreatable scanner disagreed with createNumber on edge cases; fix deletes the whole scanner and delegates to createNumber, catching RuntimeException, replacing the approach rather than extending it
split refreshed stopTimeNanos but not its wall-clock counterpart stopInstant, leaving it stale; a paired field not refreshed, fixed by an added assignment in both split overloads
deprecated getStopTime dereferenced a null stop instant, throwing NPE; null guard added as a ternary keeping the original call chain as its true branch
CEILING rounded a value already on the field boundary up to the next unit; the existing round-up condition gained originalMillis != val.getTimeInMillis() for CEILING

abbreviate with an offset near the end clamped the offset and fell through to the head-abbreviation return or the minimum-width exception; fix returns the tail directly, dropping the clamp and final conditional

sleepQuietly swallowed InterruptedException without restoring the thread's interrupt status, losing the interruption for callers; addition-only re-interrupt in the catch, read as a concurrency fault under STATE rather than OMISSION

indexOf with tolerance never matched NaN since NaN-based min/max fail every comparison; NaN guard and helper added, the other overload's existing NaN test moved behind the same guard unchanged in behaviour

short class name was derived by string-processing Class.getName(), which treats every '$' as nesting; fix walks array components and declaring classes via getSimpleName, keeping the old path only for anonymous and local classes
endIndexExclusive was clamped only from above, so a very negative end made end - start overflow to a positive size; max0 wrapping in nine overloads is a transformation, not a preserved guard

recursive style descended into Number subclasses, AtomicBoolean and MutableBoolean, printing their internals; the existing wrapper and String filter, moved into accept(), gained those clauses plus a null check
ClassNotFoundException reported the last mangled candidate name instead of the requested class name; wrong variable passed to the exception constructor
letters-only or digits-only request over a range holding no such character looped forever; two scan-and-throw blocks added; the -12 are the numbers-to-digits rename and re-wraps, so addition-only

empty-marker shortcut returned substring(str, 0, maxWidth), ignoring offset, and a null marker skipped abbreviation; fix removes the shortcut and normalises null to empty, rewriting degenerate-marker handling rather than extending it

isParsable's hand-written scanner disagreed with the JDK parsers it names (e.g. '.' accepted); rewrite delegates to them, but the javadoc reverses the documented exclusion of scientific notation, so possibly a feature.
shuffle(array, random) overloads dereferenced a null array or Random; the same null guard, now documented as a no-op, added to all nine overloads, addition-only and one fault.
